key.name: start-at-login
key.description: When false, Froonty waits after login with only a top bar icon; clicking it or pressing the toggle shortcut starts it. Screen unlocks keep the current state.

key.name: island-enabled
key.description: When false, the island and all its services are torn down while the extension stays enabled.

key.name: hide-panel-clock
key.description: Makes GNOME's top bar clock transparent so the island replaces it visually. The clock stays in place so its calendar menu keeps working.

key.name: hover-open-delay
key.summary: Open the island after hovering it this long (ms)
key.description: 0 turns opening on hover off; clicking always works.

key.name: toggle-shortcut
key.summary: Keyboard shortcut to expand or collapse the island

key.name: hub-last-tab
key.description: The feature id shown when the island expands (see features/registry.js). When that tab is gone or turned off, the first tab that is on.

key.name: prefs-page
key.summary: Internal: the settings tab to show next
key.description: Set by a tab's "Open Settings" button; the settings window shows that tab and empties this key.

key.name: settings-window-view
key.description: Set by the Shell before it opens the settings window, and kept in step by the window: "settings" for the settings tabs, "all-notes" for the All notes page.

key.name: panic-buttons
key.description: At most 5 ids from panic/catalog.js; unknown ids are ignored.

key.name: notifications-enabled
key.description: GNOME's own notifications, newest first, urgent ones on top: click one to open it (GNOME's rule: for an app that gave it no default action, GNOME opens the app and removes all of that app's non-resident notifications), × dismisses it, Clear all (after a confirmation) dismisses them all. Froonty keeps no copy, watches them only while the tab is on screen, and never removes one on its own. Do Not Disturb is GNOME's org.gnome.desktop.notifications show-banners.

key.name: notifications-width
key.description: In logical pixels, while the Notifications tab is shown.

key.name: notifications-height
key.description: In logical pixels, while the Notifications tab is shown.

key.name: notes-folder
key.description: Folder holding one Markdown file per note. Empty: ~/.local/share/froonty/notes.

key.name: notes-wrap
key.description: Off: lines stay on one line and the note scrolls horizontally.

key.name: notes-show-tools
key.summary: Show the formatting row in notes
key.description: Off: the row with the formatting buttons, line wrap and note colour is folded away (⤵ after "+" unfolds it), leaving more room for the note.

key.name: notes-width
key.description: In logical pixels, while the Notes tab is shown.

key.name: notes-height
key.description: In logical pixels, while the Notes tab is shown.

key.name: notes-label-match
key.summary: All notes: how selected labels filter
key.description: "all": notes that have every selected label; "any": notes that have at least one.

key.name: claude-enabled
key.description: Claude plan usage (session, weekly, weekly per model, cloud session credits) and when each resets, as Claude Code last checked it. Froonty reads Claude Code's config file and what its own Claude Code status line saved; it never signs in to Claude itself.

key.name: zerotier-enabled
key.description: Whether ZeroTier runs, starts with the computer and reaches its networks, and how each joined network is doing. Turned off on Froonty's first start when ZeroTier is not installed.

key.name: zerotier-install-checked
key.description: Set on Froonty's first start, once it has turned the ZeroTier tab off if ZeroTier is not installed, so that check is not repeated.

key.name: claude-ask-claude-code
key.summary: Ask Claude Code for fresh usage
key.description: When the Claude tab or its panic button comes on screen, run Claude Code's /usage (at most once a minute) so its usage cache is current. Off: only Froonty's Claude Code status line updates Session and Weekly. Froonty turns this off as Power Saver mode or a battery below 20% (on battery) begins, and back on as it ends if it was Froonty that turned it off; turning it on meanwhile is kept.

key.name: claude-ask-paused-for-power
key.summary: Internal: fresh usage turned off for low power
key.description: Set while Froonty has turned claude-ask-claude-code off for low power, so it turns it back on when low power ends.

key.name: claude-low-power-handled
key.summary: Internal: the current low power was acted on
key.description: Set from the start of a low-power stretch to its end, so turning claude-ask-claude-code back on during it is kept.

key.name: claude-attention-enabled
key.summary: Show a bar under the island when Claude needs you
key.description: A slim bar under the collapsed island while a Claude session waits for you (a permission, a question, a finished reply), from Claude Code's hooks (after Set up in Settings → Claude) and the Claude app's own notifications. Event-driven: nothing is polled. Turning it off removes its folder under $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/froonty.

key.name: claude-attention-finished
key.description: Finished replies (Claude Code's Stop hook, the Claude app's "finished" notification) and replies stopped by an error, unless you are looking at that window.

key.name: claude-attention-app
key.summary: Sessions in the Claude app from its own notifications
key.description: On: the Claude app's own notifications stand for its sessions, and Claude Code's hooks from the app are ignored. Off: the hooks are used for them too.

key.name: claude-attention-browsers
key.description: Best effort: a notification from a web browser (an app in the WebBrowser category) whose title or text contains "claude.ai".

key.name: sysmon-enabled
key.description: CPU, graphics cards, memory, disks and network, read while the tab is on screen and not at all otherwise.

key.name: sysmon-interval
key.description: How often the Btop tab reads the machine while it is on screen.

key.name: sysmon-show-cpu
key.description: Model, clock, temperature and load; each thread in a fold-out.

key.name: sysmon-show-gpu
key.description: Each card's load, temperature, power and memory, as far as its driver reports them. NVIDIA cards are read with nvidia-smi, and never while asleep.

key.name: sysmon-show-disks
key.description: Root file system, swap and the EFI system partition.

key.name: sysmon-show-network
key.description: Download and upload speed and totals, over physical interfaces only.

key.name: sysmon-width
key.description: In logical pixels, while the Btop tab is shown. Below 460, each thread takes a row of its own.

key.name: sysmon-height
key.description: In logical pixels, while the Btop tab is shown.

key.name: media-enabled
key.description: What music and video players report over MPRIS on the session bus, with play, pause, skip and seek. Needs no extra packages.

key.name: media-width
key.description: In logical pixels, while the Media tab is shown.

key.name: media-height
key.description: In logical pixels, while the Media tab is shown. Lyrics and Up next add 224 while open.

key.name: media-show-in-pill
key.description: The cover and moving bars beside the time on the collapsed island while a song plays.

key.name: media-track-notice
key.description: The collapsed island shows a new song's title and artist for 3 seconds.

key.name: media-pill-opens-tab
key.summary: Media: open the Media tab from the island
key.description: Clicking (or hovering open) the collapsed island while it shows music opens the Media tab.

key.name: media-animate-bars
key.description: While music plays, the bars beside the time and the title move. GNOME then redraws that small area every frame. GNOME's own "Animations" switch also stops them.

key.name: media-gestures
key.description: Two fingers left (next) or right (previous) on the touchpad, over the music on the island or the Media tab's player.

key.name: media-include-other-players
key.summary: Media: follow browsers and video players automatically
key.description: When off, browsers and video players show only when chosen in the tab; music players are always followed. On by default because much music plays in a browser, and a browser cannot be told apart from a music app over MPRIS.

key.name: media-remote-art
key.summary: Media: cover art from the internet
key.description: Some players give their cover as a web address; when on, Froonty downloads it from that address (no cookies, no cache on disk). Off by default.

key.name: media-lyrics
key.description: A Lyrics button in the Media tab: the player's own lyrics, or a .lrc file next to a local song.

key.name: media-lyrics-online
key.description: When no lyrics are on this computer, look them up on lrclib.net, which receives the song's title, artist, album and length. Off by default.

key.name: media-queue
key.description: An Up next button in the Media tab: the player's upcoming songs, for players that share them (MPRIS TrackList).

key.name: clipboard-enabled
key.summary: Show the Clipboard tab and record clipboard history
key.description: While on, Froonty keeps what you copy or cut (text, images, file and folder locations) in a history on this computer only (~/.local/share/froonty/clipboard, readable by you only), so it can be copied again. Passwords are never saved: copies marked secret by password managers, copies made while an app in clipboard-ignored-apps has the focus, and (clipboard-detect-passwords) text that looks like a password. Off by default.

key.name: clipboard-history-size
key.description: Older entries are deleted, with their images.

key.name: clipboard-ignored-apps
key.summary: Clipboard history: apps whose copies are never kept
key.description: Matched, ignoring case, against the focused app's desktop id and name, its window class and its Flatpak app id; "keepass" covers org.keepassxc.KeePassXC. Password managers and authenticators by default.

key.name: clipboard-password-minutes
key.summary: Clipboard history: minutes a copied password is shown, hidden
key.description: A copied password is never saved. The latest one is listed as •••••••• (in memory only) and can be copied again until these minutes pass, the clipboard is cleared or something else is copied, whichever comes first. 0: passwords are not listed at all.

key.name: clipboard-detect-passwords
key.summary: Clipboard history: treat text that looks like a password as one
key.description: Browsers' password managers do not mark their copies, so one word of 8-64 characters mixing at least three of lower case, upper case, digits and symbols (and not a link, path, date, hash or code name) is treated as a password: never saved, only shown hidden.

key.name: clipboard-width
key.description: In logical pixels, while the Clipboard tab is shown.

key.name: clipboard-height
key.description: In logical pixels, while the Clipboard tab is shown.

key.name: calendar-enabled
key.description: The events of the calendars GNOME knows (Settings → Online Accounts, GNOME Calendar, Evolution), read-only from Evolution Data Server. Needs gir1.2-ecal-2.0; turned off once, on the first start, when it is missing.

key.name: calendar-eds-checked
key.summary: Calendar: the first-start check for gir1.2-ecal-2.0 ran (internal)

key.name: calendar-hidden-sources
key.summary: Calendar: calendars hidden in the tab
key.description: Evolution Data Server source ids. Every calendar GNOME's own calendar shows is in the tab unless listed here.

key.name: calendar-granularity
key.summary: Calendar: the span the agenda shows
key.description: "day", "week" or "month" around the selected day. Chosen in the tab.

key.name: calendar-width
key.description: In logical pixels, while the Calendar tab is shown.

key.name: calendar-height
key.description: In logical pixels, while the Calendar tab is shown.

key.name: killprocess-enabled
key.description: All of your own processes, sorted by CPU load, memory or threads, each with a kill button (a click, then a confirmation; SIGTERM, then "Force quit" with SIGKILL if it is still running a few seconds later). GNOME Shell, whatever started it, and session programs are never offered. Read from /proc only while the tab is on screen. Off by default.

key.name: killprocess-interval
key.description: How often the Kill Process tab reads the processes while it is on screen.

key.name: killprocess-sort
key.description: "cpu": most CPU load first; "memory": most memory first; "threads": most threads first. Ties go to the busier process. Chosen with the toggles in the tab.

key.name: killprocess-width
key.description: In logical pixels, while the Kill Process tab is shown.

key.name: killprocess-height
key.description: In logical pixels, while the Kill Process tab is shown.

key.name: break-enabled
key.summary: Show the Break tab and follow GNOME's break reminders
key.description: While on, Froonty shows GNOME's own break reminders (Settings → Wellbeing, org.gnome.desktop.break-reminders) in the island and drives them (Take, Delay, Skip); GNOME keeps the timing. It records only when you were at the computer or away, and daily totals, on this computer only (~/.local/share/froonty/break, readable by you only). It never turns GNOME's breaks on by itself: the tab offers it. Off by default. Not medical advice.

key.name: break-pill-reminders
key.summary: Break: remind in the island instead of GNOME's notifications
key.description: While the Break tab is on, GNOME's breaks are on and the island is shown, Froonty turns off GNOME's Wellbeing notifications (org.gnome.desktop.notifications.application, gnome-wellbeing-panel, enable; this also hides GNOME's daily screen-time limit alerts) and each break type's countdown, and turns back on what it changed when this, the Break tab, the island or Froonty is turned off. It keeps them off under the lock screen. Should Froonty be removed while it is not running: gsettings reset org.gnome.desktop.notifications.application:/org/gnome/desktop/notifications/application/gnome-wellbeing-panel/ enable

key.name: break-pill-cue
key.summary: Break: cue on the collapsed island
key.description: "icon": an icon after the time while a break is near, due, overdue or urgent, or a posture switch is due (each level has its own shape: ring, bare icon, round badge, wide badge with "!"); "icon-and-time": the same with the minutes, and the minutes to the next break when all is fine; "off": none (GNOME then reminds). The island never opens by itself.

key.name: break-escalate-after-skips
key.summary: Break: overdue after this many skips or delays in a row
key.description: A due break of a type skipped or delayed this many times in a row shows as overdue at once (Froonty's rule). 0: never.

key.name: break-max-delays
key.summary: Break: delays in a row, at most
key.description: The Break tab hides its Delay button after this many delays in a row of a type. 0: no limit. GNOME's own notification (shown when Froonty does not remind) keeps its Delay button.

key.name: break-make-up-time
key.summary: Break: suggest making up skipped movement time
key.description: After a skipped movement break, the suggested length of the next one grows by the skipped length, at most twice GNOME's length (a heuristic; GNOME's own length is never changed).

key.name: break-long-rest
key.description: After break-long-rest-after-minutes at the computer without an away of break-long-rest-minutes, the cue shows "urgent" and the tab suggests a long rest (Froonty's rule, after the AOA's "15 minutes after two hours"; expert opinion). Works with GNOME's breaks off too.

key.name: break-long-rest-after-minutes
key.summary: Break: long rest after (min) at the computer
key.description: Time at the computer (not counting aways of 2 minutes or more) since the last long rest.

key.name: break-long-rest-minutes
key.description: An away at least this long (idle, locked or suspended) counts as a long rest.

key.name: break-exercises
key.description: Workrave's pictures and texts (GPL-3.0-or-later): a stretch when a movement break is near or due, eye exercises (comfort only) when an eye break is due.

key.name: break-history-days
key.summary: Break: days of history to keep
key.description: One record per day with any activity: time at the computer, longest stretch, breaks taken, delayed and skipped, long rests, standing time and target. 98 days is GNOME's own 14 weeks.

key.name: break-width
key.description: In logical pixels, while the Break tab is shown.

key.name: break-height
key.description: In logical pixels, while the Break tab is shown.

key.name: break-gnome-saved
key.description: JSON: for each GNOME key Froonty set (the Wellbeing notifications' enable, the break types' countdown), its own earlier value (or null when it had none) and the value Froonty set, so it can restore exactly that, and leave a key the user changed since. Empty when nothing is changed.

key.name: posture-enabled
key.description: A Sitting/Standing switch in the Break tab (and an optional panic button) for a desk with a manual lever. Standing time counts only while you use the computer. Off by default.

key.name: posture-target-minutes
key.summary: Break: daily standing target (min), the minimum
key.description: The base target: 2 h is a starting minimum from an expert statement (Buckley et al. 2015). "Just the minimum today" in the tab keeps today at this, whatever the build-up.

key.name: posture-buildup
key.summary: Break: build the standing target up
key.description: Adds posture-buildup-step-minutes after you meet the target on 4 of your last 5 working days (an hour or more at the computer, not "just the minimum" days), at most once a week, up to posture-buildup-ceiling-minutes. It never steps down by itself. Off: the target is always posture-target-minutes.

key.name: posture-buildup-ceiling-minutes
key.summary: Break: build the target up to (min)
key.description: Buckley et al. 2015 suggest eventually 4 h of standing and light activity; studies of people who stand a lot link more with circulation and low-back problems (observational and uncertain).

key.name: posture-buildup-target
key.description: Where the build-up has got to; 0 (or less than posture-target-minutes): not built up yet. Settings → Break → "Reset build-up" resets it.

key.name: posture-reminders
key.summary: Break: remind to switch between sitting and standing
key.description: A cue on the island after posture-sit-minutes sitting (none once today's target is met) or posture-stand-minutes standing at the computer. It stays until you switch, choose "Not now" or step away for 2 minutes or more.

key.name: posture-sit-minutes
key.summary: Break: stand up after sitting this long (min)

key.name: posture-stand-minutes
key.summary: Break: sit down after standing this long (min)

key.name: writing-enabled
key.description: Paraphrase, fix grammar, shorten, change the tone of, or summarise text with the engines switched on below. Text leaves the computer only on a click of one of these actions, and only to the engine named above the text box. Off by default.

key.name: writing-engine
key.summary: Writing: engine chosen last in the tab
key.description: When it is switched off, the first engine switched on is used.

key.name: writing-claude-code-enabled
key.description: Your own Claude Code, run headless with every tool, MCP server, skill, hook and settings file off, on your Claude plan (Pro, Max, Team or Enterprise); API billing is refused. Counts toward your plan's usage limits. Off: it is not shown in the tab.

key.name: writing-claude-code-model
key.description: "haiku" (the lightest on your plan's usage) or "sonnet" (with low effort).

key.name: writing-languagetool-enabled
key.description: Fix grammar sends the text to LanguageTool's free public service (api.languagetool.org): no account, no key, at most 20 KB per text, and at most 10 texts a minute from Froonty. Off: it is not shown in the tab.

key.name: writing-languagetool-variants
key.description: Comma-separated, such as en-GB or pt-BR: which variant LanguageTool assumes when it detects the language. An invalid value is not sent.

key.name: writing-ollama-enabled
key.description: A model running on this computer through Ollama (127.0.0.1 only); the text never leaves the computer. Off: it is not shown in the tab.

key.name: writing-ollama-model
key.description: A model downloaded in Ollama, such as llama3.2:3b. Ollama's cloud models are never used.

key.name: writing-width
key.description: In logical pixels, while the Writing tab is shown.

key.name: writing-height
key.description: In logical pixels, while the Writing tab is shown.

key.name: show-date
key.summary: Show the date in the collapsed island

key.name: clock-format
key.description: "system" follows org.gnome.desktop.interface clock-format.

key.name: collapsed-width
key.description: Minimum. While the top bar clock is hidden, the pill grows to cover its button completely.

key.name: collapsed-height
key.description: Minimum. While the top bar clock is hidden, the pill grows to cover its button completely.

key.name: expanded-width
key.description: The open island's width while no tab is on (each tab has a size of its own). It grows when the top row needs the room.

key.name: expanded-height
key.description: The open island's height while no tab is on (each tab has a size of its own).

key.name: corner-radius
key.description: Clamped to half the current island height.

key.name: animation-duration
key.description: GNOME's global "enable-animations" and slow-down settings still apply.
